title: Uber Aims for Tens of Thousands of Robotaxis by 2028 to Offset Driver Shortages
summary:
The company will target the deployment of its autonomous fleet in more than 50 cities starting in 2028 as part of a roughly $10 billion investment in robotaxis. Uber plans to have around 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform by the end of 2026 and over 2,000 by 2027. The expansion follows comments from CEO Dara Khosrowshahi that growth in international markets has been hindered by "tighter driver availability," with the company now investing significantly to recruit more drivers and couriers to meet demand.

Uber reported third quarter revenue of $14.8B and adjusted earnings per share of $0.88, both of which topped analyst estimates. Gross bookings rose 20% year-on-year to a record $59.82B, marking a five-quarter streak of at least 20% growth. For the fourth quarter, the rideshare giant expects non-GAAP EPS between $0.95 and $0.99 and projects gross bookings to reach as much as $65.25B.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Uber has also committed about $10 billion to driverless vehicles
selectedTweets.text:
My My My $UBER!

10.8 million drivers and now Uber said tighter driver availability held back growth overseas and that it's "investing significantly" to bring more drivers on.

Uber has also committed about $10 billion to driverless vehicles. It expects around 700 fully driverless cars on the app by year-end and over 2,000 by the end of 2027.

In Dara Khosrowshahi's own words on the call: "the real goal is to get to tens of thousands of vehicles in 2028 and beyond."

My take.... recruit the drivers now, replace them later.

This is the pattern I've been tracking for years. Companies are leaning on workers to hit this quarter's numbers while they build the thing that's meant to need fewer of them.
